question: Farmers’ protests against rising costs in the agricultural sector and falling prices for their produce are spreading across the EU. The Commission’s reaction to the protests in late January was to propose to allow Member States to extend by one more year the derogation of good agricultural and environmental conditions (GAEC) standard 8 on devoting a minimum share of arable land to non-productive areas or features.

That means that the only policy response from the Commission so far has been a further weakening of the environmental rules that are key to encouraging biodiversity and protecting soil health. However, the underlying causes of farmers’ intense unease go beyond their need for more flexibility in environmental rules.

Mounting debt, extreme weather events, and especially pressure from retailers and agrochemical companies, as well as foreign imports in the context of EU free-trade deals, are key concerns for the sector. 1.
In the light of this, is the Commission reconsidering its trade policy and in particular the process to finalise the Association Agreement with Mercosur?

Would the Commission consider anticipating the evaluation of Directive (EU) 2019/633 on unfair trading practices in business-to-business relationships in the agricultural and food supply chain1and assessing its revision before 2025?
OJ L 111, 25.4.2019, p. 59.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.3.2024) In the negotiations with Mercosur, the Commission reconciled the need to make meaningful concessions to our partners with the imperative of safeguarding the interests of European farmers, while at the same time opening up important export opportunities for European agrifood products such as dairy, processed foods, wines, spirits and potatoes.

This was done, notably in sensitive sectors such as beef, poultry and sugar, by considering long liberalisation periods and using Tariff Rate Quotas (TRQs), which only allow imports of limited volumes at preferential tariff rates. These concessions represent a small fraction of EU consumption and most of them are phased-in gradually.

The agreement also provides for general bilateral safeguards that are applicable to all products, including agricultural ones, even those subject to TRQs. It includes clear commitments to responsible business conduct and corporate social responsibility practices, upholding high environmental and labour standards and to effective implementation of relevant international standards.

The Commission continues negotiating with Mercosur to ensure that the Agreement delivers on the EU’s sustainability goals. The Commission, in line with its legal obligation under Article 12(1) of Directive (EU) 2019/6331, has recently initiated the evaluation of Directive (EU) 2019/6332.

The evaluation will be used to examine, inter alia, the effectiveness of implementation measures at national level, as well as the effectiveness of cooperation between national enforcement authorities, and will serve as a basis for the report to be submitted by the Commission to the European Parliament and the Council by 1 November 2025.

The Commission is preparing, ahead of the March 2024 Agriculture and Fisheries Council, actions to improve the position of farmers in the food chain and protect them against unfair trading practices, which will cover issues such as, for instance, greater market transparency and the strengthening of trust within the supply chain.
